# THEORYs with `tags` `ecology`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Ecology** — how organisms interact with each other and their environment — symbiosis and host–microbe partnerships, competition, herbivory and trophic interactions, community structure, resilience and regime shifts in ecosystems (ADR-028). How a partner comes to live inside another and depend on it is endosymbiosis (ADR-055).

| [THEORY-128](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-128.md) | Coral recovery needs herbivores to curb algae | Hughes et al. (2007), [LIT-711](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-711.md). On the reef crest at Orpheus Island after the 1998 bleaching, four roofless cages kept large and medium fishes out of 25 m² plots for 30 months. Macroalgae averaged 56% cover inside against 4.1% and 1.7% in controls. Coral cover reached 7.7% inside against 19.2% and 20.2%, with recruitment about two-thirds lower and mortality of established colonies more than double. Control recovery came mainly from recruits of taxa bleaching had removed. Proposed: one site, four replicates, plot scale, and fish exclusion standing in for herbivore exclusion. The algal state vanished within 30 days of reopening. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-130](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-130.md) | Bleaching is exchange breakdown by many routes | Two reviews, with no data of their own. Boilard et al. | [THEORY-132](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-132.md) | Stability and resilience are distinct, can trade | Holling (1973), [LIT-741](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-741.md). Stability is return to equilibrium. Resilience is persistence under change, set by the extent of the domain of attraction and the system's distance from its edge. Budworm forests and insect populations in harsh climates are unstable and resilient; homogeneous lakes are stable and fragile. Active for the distinction, which has become standard. The claim that management for constancy erodes resilience rests on suggestive cases. | Active |
| [THEORY-136](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-136.md) v6 | Abrupt change doesn't show alternative states | Scheffer & Carpenter (2003), [LIT-726](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-726.md). Alternative attractors predict sudden shifts, multimodal states and dual responses to a driver, and so do discontinuous drivers and threshold responses. Discriminating evidence is experimental: different starting states reaching different end states, temporary disturbances causing lasting shifts, or hysteresis. Slow recovery can mimic all three. Positive feedback must be strong to produce alternative states. Active as a methodological standard. | Active |
| [THEORY-469](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-469.md) | Evolutionary niche isn't Hutchinson's niche | Trappes (2021), [LIT-169](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-169.md), read in [NOTE-155](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-155.md). The non-identity follows from a conceptual argument the reading grades strong. The three kinds of case that populate the gap are weaker: habitat degradation rests on a projected persistence failure, commensalism on one field study after the author's first candidate failed, and non-limiting resources on a "possible example". The result is scoped to Odling-Smee, Laland & Feldman's 2003 niche concept and to the externalist reading of selection pressure. It does not say the two niches differ much; they "still coincide to a large extent". | Active |
| [THEORY-473](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-473.md) | Individual niche is mostly counterfactual | Takola & Schielzeth (2022), [LIT-127](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-127.md), read in full in [NOTE-170](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-170.md). The working definition (p. 5) gives the individualized niche an absolute-fitness boundary, expected LRS ≥ 1, and splits it into realized, potential, time-slice, prospective and trajectory-based niches. That the realized niche is a point and the potential niche unobservable follows from the definitions. The paper concedes there is "no empirical solution" at the individual level (p. 15), and its fix, marginalizing fitness functions across individuals, is schematic. It is a framework for structuring research, by its authors' own account, not a measurement. | Active |

| [THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md) v2 | Leaky functions are lost by individual selection | Morris, Lenski & Zinser (2012), [LIT-1568](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1568.md), read in [NOTE-1212](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1212.md). A loss-of-function mutant invades when its resource saving B = (Q_A − Q_M)/Q_A exceeds its cost C, which falls as other cells' leaky activity protects it. Because protection falls as producers become rare, the loss is frequency dependent and stops short of community-wide loss. The evidence is Prochlorococcus's loss of katG and its dependence on a peroxide-removing community. The dependence it produces is one-way, from beneficiaries to helpers, and involves no collective. | Active |

| [THEORY-1834](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1834.md) | Climate pulses birth and kill fairy circles | Zelnik, Meron & Bel (2015), [LIT-2550](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2550.md), read in [NOTE-1909](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1909.md). Hybrid states are shown by numerical continuation, and the cascade and its dependence on the start by simulation. The field side is correlations over eight images, with one birth and one death illustrated. The sharp edge: D_W is set above the authors' own estimated range to stand for termites; the pulses are idealized; and real rainfall variability would, the authors concede, push the simplified model to a uniform state. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1957](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1957.md) | Property rights unbundle into five rights | Schlager & Ostrom (1992), [LIT-2761](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2761.md), read in [NOTE-2062](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2062.md). Five rights at two levels and four positions; collective-choice rights mark "the difference between exercising a right and participating in the definition of future rights to be exercised"; a constitutional level devises collective-choice rules. It corroborates the structural premise of [CLAIM-727](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-727.md), which does not rest on it (authority at one level does not carry the next), and bears on [QUESTION-481](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-481.md). The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2231.md) | Hodgkinia split six times in Tettigades | Łukasik, Nazario, Van Leuven, Campbell, Meyer, Michalik, Pessacq, Simon, Veloso & McCutcheon (2017/2018), [LIT-1586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1586.md), read in [NOTE-2321](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2321.md). The authors also speculate, without testing, that splitting is nonadaptive for the host, begets more splitting, and makes the symbiont population harder to control; that reading is theirs and is not what this entry asserts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2232](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2232.md) | Hodgkinia split differently in each cicada | Campbell, Łukasik, Simon & McCutcheon (2017), [LIT-1602](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1602.md), read in [NOTE-2322](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2322.md). The authors read the lack of convergence as evidence that the host does not dictate the splitting and that it is nonadaptive for the host; that reading is theirs. Not shown: whether the circles are separate cells. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2287.md) v2 | Coexistence needs fitness ratio within overlap | Chesson (2011), restating his 1990 reworking of MacArthur. With consumption rates c_jl, resource values v_l, carrying capacities K_l, renewal rates r_l and maintenance requirements μ_j, define s_j = √(Σ_l c_jl² v_l K_l / r_l), κ_j = (Σ_l c_jl K_l v_l − μ_j)/s_j and ρ = Σ_l c_jl v_l K_l c_kl / r_l / (s_j s_k). Then κ_j ρ / κ_i = α_ij/α_jj, and two species coexist when ρ < κ₁/κ₂ < 1/ρ. The overlap is unaffected by the heights of the consumption curves, which go into κ. Stable coexistence means each species recovers from low density; neutral models are ρ = 1 with equal κ. | Active |
